# About

Markdown inside cells is preserved and HTML is escaped for you, so
*emphasis*, `code`, and a literal `<tag>` all come out right. Ordinary
paragraphs, like this one, need no `.entries` div at all.

# Employment

Each row of the table is one entry, and each column is a field on it. The
`detailed` style puts `with` (the employer) in the heading, with an optional
row of `tags` badges alongside it, and `what` (the job title) underneath. A
grid table cell can hold a bullet list, so `tags` and `why` each carry
several items per entry — one badge per `tags` bullet, one point per `why`
bullet.

::: {.entries style="detailed"}
+------------+------------------------------------+-----------+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| what       | with                               | when      | tags                   | why                                            |
+============+====================================+===========+========================+================================================+
| Professor  | University of Paris                | 1906-1934 | - Radiochemistry       | - First woman to hold the chair                |
|            |                                    |           | - Teaching             |   of General Physics                           |
|            |                                    |           |                        | - Directed the Curie Laboratory                |
+------------+------------------------------------+-----------+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
| Researcher | [EPCI](https://www.espci.psl.eu/)  | 1897-1906 | - Radiometry           | - Isolated polonium and radium                 |
+------------+------------------------------------+-----------+------------------------+------------------------------------------------+
:::

# Education

Where your data uses different headings, rename them with `fields`, written
`new: old` in the manner of `dplyr::rename()`.

::: {.entries style="detailed" fields="{what: Degree, with: Institution, when: Years}"}
| Degree             | Institution          | Years     |
|--------------------|-----------------------|-----------|
| Ph.D. in Physics   | University of Paris  | 1891-1895 |
| M.Sc. in Chemistry | University of Paris  | 1889-1891 |
:::

# Awards

The `brief` style is a single line per entry, for a list that needs no
elaboration.

::: {.entries style="brief"}
| what                     | where            | when |
|--------------------------|-------------------|------|
| Nobel Prize in Chemistry | Swedish Academy   | 1911 |
| Davy Medal               | Royal Society     | 1903 |
| Nobel Prize in Physics   | Swedish Academy   | 1903 |
:::

# Skills

The `skills` style pairs a category with its members, written either as one
string in `with` or as a list in `why`. For a flat wall of pills with no
categories, use `badges` instead.

::: {.entries style="skills" collapse="why"}
| what        | why                                  |
|-------------|----------------------------------------|
| Techniques  | Fractional crystallisation             |
| Techniques  | Piezoelectric quartz electrometry      |
| Techniques  | Radiometric measurement                |
:::

::: {.entries style="skills"}
| what      | with                     |
|-----------|--------------------------|
| Languages | Polish, French, Russian |
:::

# Side projects

The `cards` style lays entries out in a responsive grid, for a showcase
listing rather than a chronological one. Write `what` as a markdown link to
make the card title clickable, and `tags` as a bullet list for a row of
separate badges.

::: {.entries style="cards"}
+--------------------------------------------------+----------------------+------------------------------------------+
| what                                             | tags                 | why                                      |
+==================================================+======================+==========================================+
| [Radioactivity Discovery](https://example.org)   | - Physics            | Announced the discovery of a new         |
|                                                  | - Publication        | radioactive element in pitchblende.      |
+--------------------------------------------------+----------------------+------------------------------------------+
| Mobile X-ray units                               | - Engineering        | Designed and drove mobile radiography    |
|                                                  | - Wartime medicine   | units to treat wounded soldiers.         |
+--------------------------------------------------+----------------------+------------------------------------------+
:::
